prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Miami. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Miami for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — to give specific practices I’ll need a bit more info so I pick offices that are convenient and appropriate for your case. Quick questions:

- What ZIP code or neighborhood in Miami are you near or willing to travel from?  
- Is this a single-tooth implant, multiple implants, or a full-arch (All-on-4/6) case?  
- Do you have dental insurance that covers implants or financing limits?  
- Any preferences for provider type (oral surgeon, periodontist, prosthodontist), sedation type (IV sedation, oral sedative, or none), or desire for same-day teeth?  
- How soon do you want the work done?

If you want suggestions now without those details, I can’t reliably name the best local offices for you, but here’s a fast, practical plan and what to call for — plus the exact questions to ask when you call so you can quickly compare offices:

Which kinds of practices to call (and why)
- Board-certified oral & maxillofacial surgeons — best for surgical complexity (bone grafts, sinus lifts, impacted teeth, general anesthesia). Call them if your case might need major surgery.
- Periodontists who place implants — experts in gum/bone health and implant placement in esthetic zones.
- Prosthodontists — specialists in implant-supported crowns, bridges and full-arch restorations; call if you want the best long-term prosthetic outcome.
- Multi-specialty implant centers / specialty dental clinics — often have surgeons + prosthodontists working together under one roof, which speeds coordination and can improve outcomes for complex/full-arch cases.
- University dental clinics (if you’re open to academic settings) — often lower cost and supervised by specialists; good for straightforward or budget-sensitive cases.

How to find reputable offices in Miami right away
- Use specialist directories: American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (AAOMS), American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID), American Academy of Periodontology (AAP), or the American College of Prosthodontists — these let you search by city/ZIP for board-certified providers.
- Check local patient reviews (Google, Yelp, Healthgrades) but weigh technical credentials more heavily than ratings alone.
- Look for offices that use CBCT (3D) imaging, guided implant planning, and have on-site lab/RESTORATIVE prosthodontist involvement.

Exact questions to ask when you call
1. Do you place dental implants? How many implant surgeries do you do per month?  
2. What is the provider’s specialty and board certification? (oral surgeon, periodontist, prosthodontist; ABOMS or other board?)  
3. Will my implant treatment be planned/restored by a prosthodontist or general dentist? Are the surgeon and restorative dentist in the same office or do you coordinate between offices?  
4. Do you use CBCT (3D) imaging and digital implant planning/guided surgery?  
5. Do you provide bone grafting/sinus lift if needed? Any additional costs likely?  
6. What sedation options do you offer and what are the costs?  
7. Do you offer same-day temporary teeth or immediate-load options? Are those recommended for my case?  
8. What is the estimated total cost from implant placement through crown (or for full-arch), and what is the typical timeline?  
9. Can I see before/after photos of similar cases and patient references?  
10. Do you offer financing or a payment plan and any implant warranty/guarantee?

If you give me your ZIP code/neighborhood and the answers to 1–2 of the bullet questions (single tooth vs full-arch, insurance/financing), I’ll compile a tailored list of 5–7 specific Miami-area practices to call, with a short reason for recommending each (specialty, reputation, services, and who each is best for).
